name: Odonto-onycho-dermal dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Odonto-onycho-dermal dysplasia

criteria.description: Hypodontia or oligodontia with conical or pegged teeth
Severe nail dystrophy or onychodystrophy affecting fingernails and toenails
Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with diffuse or focal keratoderma
Hypohidrosis or anhidrosis due to sweat gland hypoplasia
Sparse, thin, or brittle scalp hair

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (tooth anomalies, nail dystrophy, and palmoplantar keratoderma) with supportive minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for WNT10A mutations can confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic dental anomalies with missing or peg-shaped teeth
Marked nail abnormalities affecting all nails
Thickened skin on palms and soles

common.notes: Reduced or absent sweating due to sweat gland hypoplasia
Mild facial features including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia

occasional.notes: Localized excessive sweating despite overall hypohidrosis
searchTerms: excessive sweating on palms and soles
too much hand and foot sweating

occasional.notes: Keratotic skin lesions around mouth and nose
searchTerms: thickened skin around mouth and eyes
scaly skin plaques on face edges

occasional.symptomName: Dental caries due to enamel defects

rare.symptomName: Sparse or absent eyebrows and eyelashes
rare.notes: Partial or complete loss of eyebrow and eyelash hair
searchTerms: thin or missing eyebrows and eyelashes
loss of eyebrow and eyelash hair

rare.notes: Cracks or fissures in thickened skin
searchTerms: mild cracks on palms and soles
slight skin fissures on hands and feet

laboratory: Sweat chloride test normal or mildly reduced sweat production
imaging: Dental radiographs showing hypodontia and abnormal tooth morphology
other: Histopathology of skin shows hypoplastic sweat glands and hyperkeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent hypohidrosis with sparse hair
Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing and saddle nose
WNT10A mutations but with additional eyelid tumors

redFlags: Severe hypodontia leading to feeding difficulties
Progressive nail dystrophy with secondary infections
references: Cluzeau C, Hadj-Rabia S, Bal E, et al. Only four genes (EDA1, EDAR, EDARADD, and WNT10A) account for 90% of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia cases. Hum Mutat. 2011.
Adaimy L, Chouery E, Megarbane H, et al. Mutation in WNT10A is associated with an autosomal recessive ectodermal dysplasia: the odonto-onycho-dermal dysplasia. Am J Hum Genet. 2007.
